title: Animal Tissues
standard_code: Biology 2, Quarter 3: Plant and Animal Tissues
standard_text: Animal tissues: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissues, their structure, location and functions; levels of organization in animals. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 2, Quarter 3)
meta_desc: Free Biology 2 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 3): epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue, and levels of organization. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: There are four kinds of animal tissue.
body_html:
How to think about it

Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines organs; its cells are tightly packed. Connective tissue (bone, cartilage, blood, fat and tendons) supports, connects and transports.

Muscle tissue (skeletal, smooth and cardiac) contracts to move the body and organs. Nervous tissue (neurons and supporting cells) carries electrical signals. Tissues combine to form organs and organ systems.

Example

Which tissue type is blood?

Connects and transports

Answer: connective tissue

Example

Which muscle type is found only in the heart?

Never tires

Answer: cardiac muscle

Common mistakes

  • Thinking blood is not a tissue.
  • Mixing up smooth and skeletal muscle.
  • Thinking all epithelial cells look the same.

faq.q: Why are cells in the skin's epidermis tightly packed?
faq.a: To protect the body from water loss and germs.

faq.q: Why do neurons have long extensions?
faq.a: To carry signals over long distances quickly.

items.q: What is the main nitrogenous waste of a frog?
items.e: Tadpoles excrete ammonia.

items.q: Which muscle is involuntary and striated?
items.e: It has intercalated discs.

items.q: Which connective tissue has a fluid matrix?
items.e: Plasma is its matrix.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone?
items.e: Tendon: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone.

items.q: Where is cardiac muscle found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
the wall of the stomach and intestine
items.e: Cardiac muscle: the wall of the heart.

items.q: Which cells of the neural tissue support and protect neurons?
items.e: They make up more than half the volume of neural tissue.

items.q: Where is cartilage found, or what does it do?
c: the wall of the stomach and intestine
just beneath the skin, as a support framework
the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
items.e: Cartilage: the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae.

items.q: Where is blood found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Blood: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix.

items.q: Where is squamous epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Squamous epithelium: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae?
items.e: Cartilage: the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae.

items.q: How many chambers does a frog's heart have?
c: three: two atria and one ventricle
items.e: There is also a sinus venosus and conus arteriosus.

items.q: Where is smooth muscle found, or what does it do?
c: the wall of the stomach and intestine
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
connecting a bone to another bone
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Smooth muscle: the wall of the stomach and intestine.

items.q: How does fertilization take place in frogs?
c: in the egg after laying on land
items.e: Development includes a tadpole stage (metamorphosis).

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: connecting a bone to another bone?
items.e: Ligament: connecting a bone to another bone.

items.q: Where is neural tissue found, or what does it do?
c: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix
items.e: Neural tissue: carrying messages as nerve impulses.

items.q: What does a male frog have that a female does not?
c: vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb
items.e: These help the male call and hold the female.

items.q: What is the hard matrix of bone made of?
items.e: Osteocytes lie in spaces called lacunae.

items.q: Where is areolar tissue found, or what does it do?
c: the tip of the nose, the outer ear and between the vertebrae
just beneath the skin, as a support framework
items.e: Areolar tissue: just beneath the skin, as a support framework.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs?
items.e: Squamous epithelium: the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx?
items.e: Compound epithelium: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx.

items.q: Where is adipose tissue found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
items.e: Adipose tissue: storing fat below the skin.

items.q: Where is compound epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells
the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx
the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
items.e: Compound epithelium: the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the mouth and pharynx.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: just beneath the skin, as a support framework?
items.e: Areolar tissue: just beneath the skin, as a support framework.

items.q: Which glands release secretions through ducts?
items.e: e.g. salivary glands and mucus glands.

items.q: Which muscle is voluntary and striated?
items.e: It is attached to bones.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: carrying messages as nerve impulses?
items.e: Neural tissue: carrying messages as nerve impulses.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix?
items.e: Blood: transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the wall of the stomach and intestine?
items.e: Smooth muscle: the wall of the stomach and intestine.

items.q: Where is ciliated epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
just beneath the skin, as a support framework
items.e: Ciliated epithelium: the bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

items.q: Where is ligament found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
items.e: Ligament: connecting a bone to another bone.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: storing fat below the skin?
items.e: Adipose tissue: storing fat below the skin.

items.q: What do gap junctions do?
c: they connect the cytoplasm of neighboring cells for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules
items.e: Found in cardiac muscle.

items.q: How does a frog breathe in water?
c: it does not breathe in water
items.e: On land it also uses its lungs and buccal cavity.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the bronchioles and fallopian tubes?
items.e: Ciliated epithelium: the bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

items.q: Where is tendon found, or what does it do?
c: the wall of the stomach and intestine
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs
items.e: Tendon: connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the wall of the heart?
items.e: Cardiac muscle: the wall of the heart.

items.q: Where is cuboidal epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: connecting a bone to another bone
just beneath the skin, as a support framework
the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons
items.e: Cuboidal epithelium: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons.

items.q: Where is columnar epithelium found, or what does it do?
c: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells
connecting a skeletal muscle to a bone
transporting substances round the body in a fluid matrix
items.e: Columnar epithelium: the lining of the stomach and intestine, with tall cells.

items.q: Which tissue matches this description: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons?
items.e: Cuboidal epithelium: the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons.

items.q: Which junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
items.e: Gap junctions let ions and small molecules pass between cells.

items.q: What is tidal volume?
c: the volume left after breathing out
the volume of air breathed in or out in one normal breath
the maximum volume of the lungs
items.e: About 0.5 L at rest.

items.q: Which level of organization is a kidney?
items.e: A kidney is an organ.

items.q: Which level of organization is bone tissue?
items.e: Bone tissue is a tissue.

items.q: Finger bones and muscles let us write and grip. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: The spine surrounds the spinal cord. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker wall than the right ventricle?
c: it pumps blood all round the body, which needs higher pressure
it receives blood from the lungs
items.e: The right ventricle pumps only to the lungs.

items.q: A block of agar is 3 cm × 4 cm × 6 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.
A block of agar is 2 cm × 2 cm × 8 cm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio, as x : 1.
Which level of organization is a human?
items.e: A human is an organism.

items.q: Which bone holds the bottom teeth and lets us chew?
items.e: Match the bone to its job.

items.q: Kevin smells something burning in the oven. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the nose (smell).

items.q: The spine keeps us upright. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: Which organ system does the lungs belong to?
items.e: The lungs is part of the respiratory system.

items.q: A helmet of bone covers the brain. Which job of the skeleton is this?
items.e: The skeleton supports, protects and helps us move.

items.q: What does the humerus do?
c: It holds the bottom teeth and lets us chew.
It lets the arm lift and move.
It supports the body and protects organs in the lower belly.
items.e: Many bones protect soft organs.

items.q: Which bone protects the spinal cord and holds the body upright?
items.e: Match the bone to its job.

items.q: Where in the body is the skull?
items.e: Learn the main bones and where they are.

items.q: Where is most water absorbed from the gut?
c: the small intestine, with more absorbed in the large intestine
items.e: The colon absorbs the remaining water.

items.q: Joy smells smoke. Which sense organ takes in this information?
items.e: This information is taken in by the nose (smell).

items.q: Which level of organization is the digestive system?
items.e: The digestive system is an organ system.

items.q: At which level of organization is the circulatory system?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organization is the shoot system of a plant?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organization is the kidney?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organization is the heart?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organization is xylem tissue?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: A muscle cell has many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: more energy released by respiration for contraction
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which cell has many mitochondria, giving more energy released by respiration for contraction?
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: A pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes has a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body. How does this help it?
c: energy to swim to the egg
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus and a biconcave shape. How does this help it?
c: more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
energy to swim to the egg
an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: A xylem vessel has no cytoplasm or cross-walls and lignified walls. How does this help it?
c: an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
energy to swim to the egg
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a guard cell?
c: a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
items.e: A guard cell has a thicker inner wall: a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma.

items.q: A root hair cell has a long, narrow extension. How does this help it?
c: more energy released by respiration for contraction
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
energy to swim to the egg
a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: At which level of organization is a leaf?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: At which level of organization is a root hair cell?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: Which cell has no nucleus and a biconcave shape, giving more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a sperm cell?
c: no cytoplasm or cross-walls and lignified walls
a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
items.e: A sperm cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria: energy to swim to the egg.

items.q: A sperm cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
energy to swim to the egg
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a root hair cell?
c: a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
items.e: A root hair cell has a long, narrow extension: a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts.

items.q: Which cell has many chloroplasts, giving more light absorbed for photosynthesis?
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: At which level of organization is muscle tissue?
items.e: cell → tissue (similar cells) → organ (several tissues) → organ system → organism.

items.q: Which level of organization is the shoot system of a plant?
items.e: The shoot system of a plant is an organ system.

items.q: Which level of organization is a red blood cell?
items.e: A red blood cell is a cell.

items.q: Which level of organization is the lining of the stomach?
items.e: The lining of the stomach is a tissue.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for pulling your hand away from a hot stove?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which organ system does the pancreas (making insulin) belong to?
items.e: The pancreas (making insulin) is part of the endocrine system.

items.q: Which level is the largest?
items.e: An organism is made of all its systems.

items.q: What level comes right after organ system (going from small to large)?
items.e: organ system → organism.

items.q: Which organ system does the bladder belong to?
items.e: The bladder is part of the excretory (urinary) system.

items.q: Diane reads about a body system that collects information and sends messages that control the body. Which system is it?
items.e: The nervous system collects information and sends messages that control the body.

items.q: Which level of organization is the stomach?
items.e: The stomach is an organ.

items.q: What level comes right after tissue (going from small to large)?
items.e: tissue → organ.

items.q: Which level of organization is a root hair cell?
items.e: A root hair cell is a cell.

items.q: Which organ system does the heart belong to?
items.e: The heart is part of the circulatory system.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for standing up and walking?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which two systems work together most directly for moving nutrients from food to cells?
items.e: Systems interact to keep the body working.

items.q: Which organ system does the femur belong to?
items.e: The femur is part of the skeletal system.

items.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
c: cell → organ → tissue → organ system → organism
tissue → cell → organ → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
cell → tissue → organ system → organ → organism
items.e: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems.

items.q: Which organ system does the liver belong to?
items.e: The liver is part of the digestive system.

items.q: Which organ system does the white blood cells belong to?
items.e: The white blood cells is part of the immune system.

items.q: Which organ system does the brain belong to?
items.e: The brain is part of the nervous system.
